question: Which crop were peasants in Bengal forced to cultivate by European planters, leading to the revolt of 1859-60?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Indigo.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• European planters compelled Bengal cultivators to grow indigo on part of their land, and this gave rise to the Indigo Revolt of 1859-60 (नील की खेती — नील विद्रोह)

 

• The planters used the dadan system of advance, at rates fixed far below the market price, and often resorted to coercion and violence on those who refused.

 

• After the Bengal revolt, many planters shifted their operations to Bihar, where the system of tinkathia later provoked the Champaran Satyagraha of 1917.

 

• Indigo was the blue dye demanded by British textile mills, which is why European capital invested in its production.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• Opium cultivation was a government monopoly in Bihar and Malwa, linked to the China trade.

 

• The Indigo Commission, formed in 1860, found that planters had used unfair methods.

 

• Legislation passed in 1860 and the planters' own withdrawal ended the compulsory indigo system in Bengal.

 

• Bengal's indigo system shrank rapidly after 1860, and the German invention of synthetic indigo in 1897 destroyed what remained of the natural dye trade.

 

NOTE

 

• Opium (Option 1): Opium was grown under government monopoly in Bihar and Bengal for export to China, and its coercive cultivation was a different grievance from the indigo agitation of 1859-60.

 

• Cotton (Option 2): Cotton was a crop of the Deccan and Gujarat, whose price boom and bust related to the Deccan Riots of 1875, not to the Bengal planters' revolt.

 

• Jute (Option 3): Jute became a major cash crop of Bengal later in the nineteenth century for industry; it did not cause the 1859-60 revolt against forced cultivation.

question: Bhavani Pathak and Debi Chaudhurani are remembered as leaders of which revolt?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Sanyasi Revolt.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Bhavani Pathak and Debi Chaudhurani are named leaders of the Sanyasi Revolt (1763-1800) in Bengal and Bihar, along with Majnu Shah (सन्यासी विद्रोह — भवानी पाठक और देवी चौधुरानी)

 

• Debi Chaudhurani is regarded as a semi-legendary woman leader who led a band of rebels, and she appears as the title character in Bankim Chandra's novel Debi Chaudhurani (1884).

 

• The rebels were hit by the heavy British demand for revenue after Buxar (1764) and the famine of 1770, which killed about a third of Bengal's population by many estimates.

 

• This long-running movement is often called the first major peasant-linked uprising against British rule.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• Warren Hastings sent punitive forces to destroy the sanyasi bands.

 

• Anandamath, set in the background of the sanyasi struggle, also mentions Bhavani Pathak.

 

• The revolt largely ended around 1800 when organised resistance was crushed.

 

• Debi Chaudhurani was a title used by a woman who, according to tradition, led a band of boatmen-rebels along the rivers of north Bengal.

 

NOTE

 

• Kol Revolt (Option 1): The Kol Revolt of 1831-32 was a tribal rising in Chotanagpur led by Budhu Bhagat, and it neither involved sanyasis nor Bengal's fakirs and landlords.

 

• Munda Rebellion (Option 3): The Munda Rebellion of 1899-1900 was led by Birsa Munda in Ranchi region; its personalities were tribal figures and not the Bengal sanyasi leaders.

 

• Bhil Revolt (Option 4): The Bhil Revolt of 1818-46 was fought in western India under chiefs like Seva Ram, and thus is unconnected with the Bengal-Bihar sanyasi bands.

question: The Munda Rebellion (Ulgulan) took place during which period?
solution_text:
The correct answer is 1899-1900.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The Munda Rebellion (Ulgulan) under Birsa Munda took place in 1899-1900 around Ranchi on the Chotanagpur plateau (उलगुलान — 1899-1900)

 

• It ended with Birsa's arrest in early 1900 and his death in Ranchi jail in June 1900, apparently of cholera.

 

• The Ulgulan was a response to the loss of Munda land to dikus, forced labour and the erosion of the khuntkatti system.

 

• The other options give dates of the Kol Revolt, the Santhal Rebellion and the Rampa Rebellion respectively.

 

• Together with the khuntkatti land system, the loss of customary Munda rights to the dikus formed the backdrop of the movement.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• Birsa Munda was born around 1875 at Ulihatu in present-day Jharkhand.

 

• The Ulgulan prompted the Chotanagpur Tenancy Act of 1908, which recognised the khuntkatti rights of Mundas.

 

• The Mundas called Birsa Dharti Aba, meaning father of the earth.

 

• The Ulgulan's military phase started in December 1899 with arrow attacks on police stations and churches around Khunti and Tamar.

 

NOTE

 

• 1831-32 (Option 2): The years 1831-32 mark the Kol Revolt of Chotanagpur, nearly seven decades before the Birsa Munda Ulgulan, so this date is too early for the Munda uprising.

 

• 1855-56 (Option 3): The years 1855-56 mark the Santhal Rebellion led by the Murmu brothers in the Rajmahal hills; the Munda revolt happened more than forty years later.

 

• 1922-24 (Option 4): The years 1922-24 are the dates of the Rampa Rebellion of Alluri Sitarama Raju in Andhra; Birsa Munda had died in 1900, long before that period.

question: U Kiang Nangbah, hanged by the British in 1862, was a freedom fighter of which hill region?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Jaintia Hills.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• U Kiang Nangbah led the Jaintia Hills resistance against British rule and was publicly hanged at Jowai in 1862 (जयंतिया पहाड़ियाँ — यू कियांग नांगबाह)

 

• The Jaintia revolt broke out when the British imposed new taxes, including an income tax and house tax, on the Jaintia people, who were not used to such levies.

 

• The Jaintia Hills form part of the present-day state of Meghalaya, along with the Khasi and Garo hills.

 

• He is celebrated in Meghalaya as a martyr, and Jowai observes his death anniversary each December.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• The Jaintia kingdom had been annexed in 1835 after the British took the plains portion.

 

• U Tirot Sing of the Khasi Hills was another early Meghalaya hero who fought the British.

 

• Kiang Nangbah's revolt was about taxation and the loss of Jaintia self-rule, not about the opium trade.

 

• After Kiang Nangbah's execution at Jowai, the Jaintia resistance was suppressed, though his memory later inspired Meghalaya's cultural pride.

 

NOTE

 

• Naga Hills (Option 1): The Naga Hills are associated with the Heraka movement led by Jadonang and Rani Gaidinliu in the twentieth century and not with U Kiang Nangbah.

 

• Chotanagpur Plateau (Option 3): The Chotanagpur Plateau saw the Kol, Munda and Tana Bhagat movements in present-day Jharkhand; Kiang Nangbah's struggle took place in northeast India.

 

• Rajmahal Hills (Option 4): The Rajmahal Hills were the homeland of the Santhals who rose in 1855-56, far away from the Jaintia region of Meghalaya, where Kiang Nangbah resisted British taxation.

question:
Consider the following statements about the Fakir and Sanyasi uprisings:

1. The Fakir Revolt was led mainly by Muslim fakirs, with Majnu Shah as the best-known leader.

2. Hindu sanyasis, peasants and disbanded soldiers of the Bengal Nawabs also joined the rebels.

3. Both uprisings were fought in southern India against the Poligars.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Only 1 and 2.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Statement 1 is correct: the Fakir Revolt was driven by Muslim fakirs, and Majnu Shah is its most famous leader (फकीर विद्रोह — मजनू शाह)

 

• Statement 2 is correct: the rebels were joined by Hindu sanyasis, peasants and disbanded soldiers of the Bengal Nawabs, making it a broad-based resistance.

 

• Statement 3 is incorrect: both movements were fought in Bengal and Bihar, and the Poligar wars were a separate South Indian conflict in Tamil country.

 

• Their main grievances were harsh British revenue policy after the Battle of Buxar and the famine of 1770.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• Hindu-Muslim ascetic cooperation was a striking feature of these revolts.

 

• The Bengal Nawab's army had been reduced after Plassey and Buxar, throwing many soldiers out of work.

 

• Poligar resistance was led by figures such as Veerapandya Kattabomman in the late eighteenth century.

 

• Fakir bands, who wandered among villages and shrines, collected alms and used that cover to move through the countryside and rally support.

 

NOTE

 

• Only 1 and 3 (Option 2): Selecting statements 1 and 3 alone accepts the false southern location; the Fakir revolt took place in Bengal, and the Poligars of Tamil Nadu belong to a different set of conflicts.

 

• Only 2 and 3 (Option 3): Choosing only statements 2 and 3 includes the wrong geography and removes the correct identification of Majnu Shah as the leading fakir, so it is not the right combination.

 

• 1, 2 and 3 (Option 4): Accepting all three fails because statement 3 places the Fakir and Sanyasi revolts in southern India, while they were located in Bengal and Bihar.

question:
Consider the following statements about Thakkar Bappa:

1. He is credited with popularising the term Adivasi.

2. He was a member of the Servants of India Society.

3. He founded the Satyashodhak Samaj.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Only 1 and 2.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Statement 1 is correct: Thakkar Bappa (A.V. Thakkar) is credited with popularising the term Adivasi (ठक्कर बापा — आदिवासी)

 

• Statement 2 is correct: he served in Gopal Krishna Gokhale's Servants of India Society and devoted his life to social service among tribals and the depressed classes.

 

• Statement 3 is incorrect: the Satyashodhak Samaj was founded by Jyotiba Phule in Pune in 1873.

 

• Thakkar also set up the Bhil Seva Mandal in 1922 and worked with Gandhi in the Harijan Sevak Sangh.

 

• His life of service stretched from Gopal Krishna Gokhale's society to Gandhi's campaign against untouchability, and his name remains tied to work for tribal welfare.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• The Servants of India Society was founded in 1905 and was a major training ground for public workers.

 

• Phule's book Gulamgiri (1873) attacked caste oppression.

 

• Thakkar Bappa also led relief work during famines and floods.

 

• He served on the Constituent Assembly's sub-committee on excluded and partially excluded areas in 1947, a body that dealt with tribal regions.

 

NOTE

 

• Only 2 and 3 (Option 1): Choosing only statements 2 and 3 wrongly gives Thakkar credit for founding Phule's Satyashodhak Samaj, a non-Brahmin reform society of Maharashtra established in 1873.

 

• Only 1 and 3 (Option 3): Taking statements 1 and 3 together accepts the incorrect statement about the Satyashodhak Samaj, which was founded by Jyotiba Phule and has no connection with Thakkar Bappa.

 

• 1, 2 and 3 (Option 4): Accepting all three is wrong because the Satyashodhak Samaj was Jyotiba Phule's creation, so statement 3 about Thakkar cannot be correct.

question:
Consider the following statements about Jatindranath Mukherjee (Bagha Jatin):

1. He earned the title Bagha after killing a tiger with a dagger.

2. He was a revolutionary leader from Bengal.

3. He was the founder of the Indian National Army.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Only 1 and 2.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Statement 1 is correct: he gained the title Bagha (tiger) after killing a tiger with a dagger in his youth (बाघा जतिन)

 

• Statement 2 is correct: Jatindranath Mukherjee was a legendary revolutionary from Bengal, linked with the Jugantar movement, who inspired many young nationalists.

 

• Statement 3 is incorrect: the Indian National Army was first formed by Mohan Singh and Rash Behari Bose and was later led by Subhas Chandra Bose, while Jatin died in 1915.

 

• He was fatally wounded in a fight with the police at Balasore in September 1915.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• Bagha Jatin was involved in the German plot to import arms during the First World War.

 

• Rash Behari Bose, who handed the INA to Subhas Bose in 1943, had been a Bengal revolutionary of the same era.

 

• Jugantar was a prominent Bengal revolutionary society.

 

• The Anushilan Samiti, another Bengal revolutionary body, had branches at Dhaka and Calcutta, and Jatin worked with such groups to recruit young men for the cause.

 

NOTE

 

• Only 1 and 3 (Option 2): Taking statements 1 and 3 together accepts a false claim about the INA, which was established in 1942-43 during the Second World War, long after Jatindranath Mukherjee had died.

 

• Only 2 and 3 (Option 3): Joining statements 2 and 3 repeats the wrong INA claim and skips the tiger-killing origin of his title, making the combination incorrect.

 

• 1, 2 and 3 (Option 4): Accepting all three is wrong since statement 3 credits Jatin with founding the INA, which came into being in the 1940s when he was no longer alive.

question:
Consider the following statements about the Bihar Provincial Kisan Sabha:

1. It was formed in 1929.

2. Swami Sahajanand Saraswati was its founder.

3. It was established mainly to protect the interests of tea garden workers.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Only 1 and 2.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Statement 1 is correct: the Bihar Provincial Kisan Sabha was formed in 1929 (बिहार प्रांतीय किसान सभा — 1929)

 

• Statement 2 is correct: its founder was Swami Sahajanand Saraswati, who later headed the All India Kisan Sabha (1936).

 

• Statement 3 is incorrect: the Sabha aimed to protect peasants from zamindari attacks on their occupancy rights, and tea garden labour belongs to Assam, not Bihar.

 

• The Sabha campaigned against illegal levies and evictions, linking peasants' interests with the national movement.

 

• The Sabha thus was an early instance of an organised, class-based peasant platform in a province dominated by zamindars.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• The All India Kisan Sabha was founded at Lucknow in April 1936.

 

• Sahajanand Saraswati belonged to the Dasnami Sannyasi order before turning to peasant politics.

 

• Later he parted ways with the Congress over zamindari issues.

 

• The Congress later adopted agrarian programmes at the Faizpur session of 1936, a time when the peasant organisations were becoming politically influential.

 

NOTE

 

• Only 1 and 3 (Option 1): The pair of statements 1 and 3 here accepts the incorrect claim about tea garden workers, whereas the Sabha was concerned with tenant cultivators' occupancy rights against zamindars.

 

• Only 2 and 3 (Option 2): Selecting statements 2 and 3 alone drops the right year and accepts the incorrect statement; tea plantation labour was not the Kisan Sabha's main concern.

 

• 1, 2 and 3 (Option 4): Accepting all three fails since statement 3 is false; the movement was about peasants and zamindari rights, not plantation workers of the tea industry.

question: The Kol, Santhal and Munda movements of eastern India shared which common grievance?
option_1: Imposition of a salt tax on coastal tribes
option_2: Forced recruitment into the Bengal Army
option_3: Ban on the practice of sati
option_4: Loss of tribal land to outsiders (dikus) such as zamindars and moneylenders
solution_text:
The correct answer is Loss of tribal land to outsiders (dikus) such as zamindars and moneylenders.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• All three movements were driven largely by the alienation of tribal land to outsiders — zamindars, traders and moneylenders, called dikus — protected by the colonial legal and revenue system (कोल, संथाल और मुंडा — भूमि अलगाव)

 

• The Kol Revolt (1831-32) in Chotanagpur was a reaction to the transfer of tribal land to non-tribal farmers and revenue-farmers.

 

• The Santhal Rebellion (1855-56) arose from the exploitation of Santhals by zamindars, moneylenders and officials who supported them.

 

• The Munda Ulgulan (1899-1900) defended the khuntkatti system and demanded restoration of land rights against dikus.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• Colonial courts and police generally favoured the landlords and moneylenders over tribals.

 

• Repeated tribal revolts led to special tenancy laws, such as the Chotanagpur Tenancy Act of 1908 and the Santhal Parganas Tenancy provisions.

 

• The word diku means an outsider who exploits tribal people.

 

• The Santhal Parganas Tenancy Act of 1876 and the Chotanagpur Tenancy Act of 1908 were attempts to block the transfer of tribal land.

 

NOTE

 

• Imposition of a salt tax on coastal tribes (Option 1): A salt tax on coastal communities has no connection with the hill and plateau tribes of Chotanagpur and the Rajmahal hills, and salt duty was not a grievance in any of these revolts.

 

• Forced recruitment into the Bengal Army (Option 2): Forced recruitment into the Bengal Army was not the cause of these tribal movements; their anger was aimed at landlords, moneylenders and revenue officials rather than military service.

 

• Ban on the practice of sati (Option 3): The ban on sati was enacted in 1829 by Bentinck and had nothing to do with the land grievances of Kols, Santhals and Mundas.

question:
Match the revolts in Column A with their leaders in Column B.

Column A: (a) Kol Revolt (b) Santhal Rebellion (c) Munda Ulgulan (d) Rampa Rebellion

Column B: (i) Birsa Munda (ii) Budhu Bhagat (iii) Alluri Sitarama Raju (iv) Sidhu and Kanhu Murmu
solution_text:
The correct answer is a-ii, b-iv, c-i, d-iii.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The Kol Revolt (1831-32) in Chotanagpur is linked with Budhu Bhagat, so a-ii is right (विद्रोह और नेताओं का मिलान)

 

• The Santhal Rebellion (1855-56) was led by Sidhu and Kanhu Murmu, along with their brothers Chand and Bhairav, which gives b-iv.

 

• The Munda Ulgulan (1899-1900) was the movement of Birsa Munda, which gives c-i.

 

• The Rampa Rebellion (1922-24) was led by Alluri Sitarama Raju in Andhra, which gives d-iii; together these four pairs form the correct code.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• The Kol, Santhal and Munda movements all arose within the Chotanagpur-Rajmahal belt.

 

• Rampa is the only one of the four set in southern India.

 

• Alluri Sitarama Raju and Birsa Munda both died young in custody or in combat with British forces.

 

• Chotanagpur's tribal movements are among the favourite topics of examiners, and Budhu Bhagat, Sidhu-Kanhu and Birsa Munda appear again and again in question papers.

 

NOTE

 

• a-iv, b-ii, c-i, d-iii (Option 1): This code gives Sidhu and Kanhu to the Kol Revolt and Budhu Bhagat to the Santhals, which reverses two leaders; the Kol leader was Budhu Bhagat and the Santhal leaders were the Murmu brothers.

 

• a-ii, b-iv, c-iii, d-i (Option 2): This code attaches Alluri Sitarama Raju to the Munda Ulgulan and Birsa Munda to Rampa, which swaps two leaders who lived in different regions and decades.

 

• a-i, b-iv, c-ii, d-iii (Option 4): This code gives Birsa Munda to the Kol Revolt and Budhu Bhagat to the Munda Ulgulan, which wrongly exchanges the leaders of the 1831-32 and the 1899-1900 revolts.

question:
Match the revolts in Column A with their regions in Column B.

Column A: (a) Santhal Rebellion (b) Rampa Rebellion (c) Bhil Revolt (d) Indigo Revolt

Column B: (i) Western India (Khandesh) (ii) Godavari hill tracts (iii) Rajmahal Hills (iv) Nadia and other districts of Bengal
solution_text:
The correct answer is a-iii, b-ii, c-i, d-iv.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The Santhal Rebellion was fought around the Rajmahal Hills, giving a-iii (विद्रोह और क्षेत्र का मिलान)

 

• The Rampa Rebellion of Alluri Sitarama Raju took place in the Godavari hill tracts of Andhra, giving b-ii.

 

• The Bhil Revolt (1818-46) was a tribal uprising in Western India, mainly Khandesh, giving c-i.

 

• The Indigo Revolt (1859-60) occurred in Bengal, including Nadia, giving d-iv.

 

• Taken together, each pair ties a revolt to its homeland, which is why geography is a safe way to separate tribal revolts of the east from those of the west and south.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• Khandesh lies in northwestern Maharashtra.

 

• The Rampa region is often called the Godavari Agency.

 

• Nadia in West Bengal was a major centre of indigo cultivation and protest.

 

• The Poligar wars and the Rampa revolt both took place in the south, though a century and a quarter apart, and in different circumstances.

 

NOTE

 

• a-ii, b-iii, c-i, d-iv (Option 1): This code swaps the places of the Santhal and Rampa revolts; the Santhals lived in the Rajmahal hills of the east, while Rampa was in the Andhra hills far to the south.

 

• a-iii, b-i, c-ii, d-iv (Option 2): This code gives the Godavari tracts to the Bhils and western India to Rampa, which is wrong because the Bhils were a western Indian tribe and Raju fought in Andhra.

 

• a-iv, b-ii, c-i, d-iii (Option 3): This code gives Bengal to the Santhal Rebellion and Rajmahal to the Indigo Revolt, but the Santhals rose in the Rajmahal hills and indigo cultivators protested in Bengal's plains.

question:
Match the personalities in Column A with their contributions in Column B.

Column A: (a) Thakkar Bappa (b) D.K. Karve (c) Swami Sahajanand Saraswati (d) Dinabandhu Mitra

Column B: (i) Founded the first Women's University in Pune (1916) (ii) Formed the Bihar Provincial Kisan Sabha (1929) (iii) Popularised the term Adivasi (iv) Wrote Nil Darpan
solution_text:
The correct answer is a-iii, b-i, c-ii, d-iv.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Thakkar Bappa is credited with popularising the term Adivasi, giving a-iii (व्यक्तित्व और योगदान का मिलान)

 

• D.K. Karve established the first Women's University in Pune in 1916, giving b-i.

 

• Swami Sahajanand Saraswati formed the Bihar Provincial Kisan Sabha in 1929, giving c-ii.

 

• Dinabandhu Mitra wrote the play Nil Darpan (1860) on the indigo planters' oppression, giving d-iv.

 

• The four people thus represent tribal welfare, women's education, peasant organisation and literary protest, which lets us rule out the swapped pairs in the other codes.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• Karve was awarded the Bharat Ratna in 1958.

 

• Sahajanand Saraswati became president of the All India Kisan Sabha in 1936.

 

• Nil Darpan was translated into English by Michael Madhusudan Dutt.

 

• The Women's University of Karve was renamed after Nathibai Damodar Thackersey, the mother of the benefactor Sir Vithaldas Thackersey, who donated Rs 15 lakh in 1920.

 

NOTE

 

• a-i, b-iii, c-ii, d-iv (Option 2): This code gives the Women's University to Thakkar Bappa and Adivasi to Karve, which is wrong because Karve was the university founder and Thakkar the social worker among tribals.

 

• a-iii, b-ii, c-i, d-iv (Option 3): This code gives the Kisan Sabha to Karve and the Women's University to Sahajanand, which reverses their fields; Karve was an educator and Sahajanand a peasant leader.

 

• a-iv, b-i, c-ii, d-iii (Option 4): This code gives Nil Darpan to Thakkar Bappa and Adivasi to Dinabandhu Mitra, but Mitra was the Bengali playwright and Thakkar Bappa popularised the word Adivasi.

question:
Match the revolts in Column A with their periods in Column B.

Column A: (a) Sanyasi Revolt (b) Kol Revolt (c) Indigo Revolt (d) Munda Rebellion

Column B: (i) 1831-32 (ii) 1859-60 (iii) 1899-1900 (iv) 1763-1800
solution_text:
The correct answer is a-iv, b-i, c-ii, d-iii.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The Sanyasi Revolt ran from 1763 to 1800, giving a-iv (विद्रोह और काल का मिलान)

 

• The Kol Revolt took place in 1831-32, giving b-i.

 

• The Indigo Revolt is dated 1859-60, giving c-ii.

 

• The Munda Rebellion (Ulgulan) took place in 1899-1900, giving d-iii.

 

• The Sanyasi revolt is the only one among them that began in the eighteenth century, while the Kol, Indigo and Munda revolts belong to the nineteenth century.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• The four dates span about 140 years of colonial rule.

 

• The Santhal Rebellion (1855-56) falls between the Kol and Indigo revolts.

 

• The Sanyasi Revolt is the earliest of these, starting just before the Battle of Buxar.

 

• The Kol, Indigo and Munda dates fall within the nineteenth century, while the Sanyasi movement began in the eighteenth.

 

NOTE

 

• a-i, b-iv, c-ii, d-iii (Option 1): This code gives the Kol period to the Sanyasi Revolt and the long 1763-1800 period to the Kol Revolt, which is wrong since the Sanyasi revolt came more than six decades before the Kol uprising.

 

• a-iv, b-ii, c-i, d-iii (Option 2): This code swaps the Kol and Indigo periods; the Kol Revolt of 1831-32 predates the Indigo Revolt of 1859-60 by nearly three decades, so the pairing is incorrect.

 

• a-iv, b-i, c-iii, d-ii (Option 3): This code swaps the Indigo and Munda periods, but the Indigo Revolt was in 1859-60 and the Ulgulan in 1899-1900, so c-iii and d-ii are mismatched.

question:
Arrange the following in chronological order (earliest first):

(a) Santhal Rebellion

(b) Kol Revolt

(c) Rampa Rebellion

(d) Munda Ulgulan
solution_text:
The correct answer is b-a-d-c.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The Kol Revolt (1831-32) comes first in this list (कालक्रम)

 

• The Santhal Rebellion (1855-56) follows the Kol Revolt by about twenty-four years.

 

• The Munda Ulgulan of Birsa Munda belongs to 1899-1900, so it follows the Santhal revolt.

 

• The Rampa Rebellion under Alluri Sitarama Raju (1922-24) is the latest of the four; the order is therefore Kol, Santhal, Munda, Rampa.

 

• The gaps between the movements are thus about twenty-four years from Kol to Santhal, about forty-four years to Munda and about twenty-three years to Rampa.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• The first three took place in the Chotanagpur-Rajmahal belt.

 

• Rampa occurred during the national movement's non-cooperation phase.

 

• The gap between the Santhal and Munda risings is roughly four decades.

 

• A convenient marker is that the Kol, Santhal and Munda revolts came about thirty to forty years apart, while Rampa was a twentieth-century movement.

 

NOTE

 

• a-b-c-d (Option 2): This sequence places the Santhal Rebellion before the Kol Revolt and Rampa before the Munda Ulgulan; the Kol rising of 1831-32 is earlier than 1855-56, and Rampa came after 1900.

 

• b-a-c-d (Option 3): This sequence is wrong in placing Rampa (1922-24) before the Munda Ulgulan (1899-1900); the rest of its order, Kol and then Santhal, is correct.

 

• a-b-d-c (Option 4): This sequence puts the Santhal Rebellion first, though the Kol Revolt of 1831-32 came earlier; its later part, the Munda Ulgulan then Rampa, is correct.

question:
Arrange the following in chronological order (earliest first):

(a) Indigo Revolt

(b) Bihar Provincial Kisan Sabha formed

(c) Rampa Rebellion

(d) Santhal Rebellion
solution_text:
The correct answer is d-a-c-b.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The Santhal Rebellion of 1855-56 is the earliest of these events (कालक्रम)

 

• The Indigo Revolt (1859-60) comes a few years after the Santhal Rebellion.

 

• The Rampa Rebellion (1922-24) of Alluri Sitarama Raju came in the 1920s.

 

• The Bihar Provincial Kisan Sabha was formed in 1929 by Swami Sahajanand Saraswati, so it is the last; the order is Santhal, Indigo, Rampa, Kisan Sabha.

 

• The Santhal and Indigo revolts belong to the Company's last years and the Crown's first, while Rampa and the Kisan Sabha belong to the Gandhian period.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• Rampa is separated from the Kisan Sabha by only five years.

 

• The Santhal and Indigo events were separated by only about four years.

 

• All four events took place under British rule, before the Government of India Act 1935.

 

• The Bihar Provincial Kisan Sabha of 1929 came a year before Gandhi's Dandi March of 1930, which started the Civil Disobedience Movement.

 

NOTE

 

• a-d-c-b (Option 1): This sequence reverses the Santhal and Indigo events; the Santhal Rebellion of 1855-56 preceded the 1859-60 indigo protest, so beginning with Indigo is incorrect.

 

• d-a-b-c (Option 2): This sequence puts the Kisan Sabha of 1929 ahead of the Rampa Rebellion, which ended in 1924, so its final two positions are inverted even though the first two are right.

 

• d-c-a-b (Option 3): This sequence places Rampa before the Indigo Revolt, but the 1922-24 rising happened more than sixty years after the Indigo Revolt of 1859-60.

question:
Arrange the following in chronological order (earliest first):

(a) Deccan Riots

(b) Pabna Agrarian Leagues

(c) Indigo Revolt

(d) Santhal Rebellion
solution_text:
The correct answer is d-c-b-a.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The Santhal Rebellion (1855-56) is the earliest (कालक्रम)

 

• The Indigo Revolt came in 1859-60, a few years later.

 

• The Pabna Agrarian Leagues operated in 1873-76 in eastern Bengal.

 

• The Deccan Riots broke out in 1875 in Maharashtra, so the order is Santhal, Indigo, Pabna, Deccan.

 

• The first two events happened within five years while the others are separated from them and from each other by a decade or more.

 

• Pabna's tenants organised leagues, collected funds and went to court rather than fighting, whereas the Santhal rebels earlier had taken up bows and arrows against zamindars and troops.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• The Pabna and Deccan movements overlapped by about two years.

 

• The Bengal Tenancy Act of 1885 followed the Pabna agitation.

 

• The Deccan Agriculturists' Relief Act came in 1879.

 

• The Deccan Riots and the Pabna movement were both agrarian revolts that avoided attacks on British rule itself and concentrated on local oppressors.

 

NOTE

 

• c-d-b-a (Option 2): This sequence starts with the Indigo Revolt, but the Santhal Rebellion of 1855-56 predates it; the remaining order Pabna then Deccan is right.

 

• d-c-a-b (Option 3): This sequence places the Deccan Riots of 1875 before Pabna's leagues, which began in 1873, so the last two positions are inverted though the first two are right.

 

• d-b-c-a (Option 4): This sequence places the Pabna leagues before the Indigo Revolt, although Pabna began in 1873, well after the 1859-60 indigo agitation.

question:
Arrange the following in chronological order (earliest first):

(a) Death of Birsa Munda

(b) Great famine of Bengal

(c) Publication of Anandamath

(d) Battle of Buxar
solution_text:
The correct answer is d-b-c-a.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The Battle of Buxar (1764) came first (कालक्रम)

 

• The Great Bengal famine followed in 1770, deepening the distress behind the Sanyasi and Fakir revolts.

 

• Bankim's Anandamath was published in 1882, drawing on the sanyasi rebellion.

 

• Birsa Munda died in Ranchi jail in 1900, which closes the sequence.

 

• Hence the sequence runs from the Company's victory in 1764 to a famine, a novel and then a tribal leader's death, which spans over a hundred and thirty years.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• Buxar gave the Company the diwani rights in 1765.

 

• The famine of 1770 killed an estimated third of Bengal's people.

 

• Vande Mataram, from Anandamath, was sung at the 1896 Congress session.

 

• The first Congress session of 1885 and the Bengal Tenancy Act of 1885 fall in the period between the Great Famine of 1770 and Birsa Munda's death.

 

NOTE

 

• b-d-c-a (Option 1): This sequence puts the 1770 famine before the Battle of Buxar of 1764, which reverses the first two events; the later part, Anandamath then Birsa's death, is right.

 

• d-b-a-c (Option 3): This sequence places Birsa Munda's death in 1900 before the publication of Anandamath in 1882, so it inverts the last two events although the first two are correctly ordered.

 

• d-c-b-a (Option 4): This sequence places Anandamath before the 1770 famine, but the novel was written in 1882, more than a century after the famine and Buxar.

question:
Assertion (A): Alluri Sitarama Raju led the Rampa Rebellion against the British.

Reason (R): He protested against the forest laws that restricted tribal access to resources.

Choose the correct option.
option_1: Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
option_2: A is true but R is false
option_3: A is false but R is true
option_4: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
solution_text:
The correct answer is Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Assertion A is true: Alluri Sitarama Raju led the Rampa Rebellion (1922-24) in the Godavari hill region of Andhra Pradesh (रम्पा विद्रोह — वन कानूनों के विरुद्ध)

 

• Reason R is also true: the tribals were deprived of the freedom to cultivate by shifting methods and gather forest produce under the Madras Forest Act.

 

• R explains A because it was precisely this forest-law grievance that led Raju to organise tribal guerrilla bands.

 

• He was caught and shot in 1924, after which the rebellion was suppressed.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• Raju is remembered as Manyam Veerudu, hero of the jungles.

 

• Forest laws were a major tribal grievance throughout British India.

 

• The rebellion is named after the Rampa region, also called the Godavari Agency.

 

• The Rampa rebels' armed actions of 1922-24 included raids on police stations, in which the guerrillas seized rifles and ammunition for their further resistance.

 

NOTE

 

• Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A (Option 1): This option accepts both statements as true but denies that the forest-law grievance explains the revolt; in fact the restriction on forest use was its direct cause, so R does explain A.

 

• A is true but R is false (Option 2): This option calls R false, but forest regulations restricting tribal access to forest produce and podu cultivation were an actual cause of the Rampa Rebellion, so R is true.

 

• A is false but R is true (Option 3): This option calls A false, yet Alluri Sitarama Raju is firmly established as the leader of the Rampa Rebellion, so A is a correct statement.

question:
Assertion (A): Rani Gaidinliu continued the Heraka movement after the death of Jadonang.

Reason (R): She aimed to convert the movement into a mass literacy campaign among the Nagas.

Choose the correct option.
option_1: A is true but R is false
option_2: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
option_3: Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
option_4: A is false but R is true
solution_text:
The correct answer is A is true but R is false.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Assertion A is true: after the British hanged Jadonang in 1931, Rani Gaidinliu carried on the Heraka movement among the Nagas (हेराका आंदोलन — रानी गाइदिन्ल्यू)

 

• Reason R is false: the movement was a religious and political revival that resisted British rule and missionary influence and aimed to preserve Naga traditions, and not a literacy drive.

 

• She was arrested in 1932 and kept in jail until 1947, and Nehru gave her the title Rani.

 

• Hence only the assertion holds.

 

• Gaidinliu's goal was to resist the British and Christian missions and to restore the Naga religion, and so a literacy campaign was never her aim.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• Heraka means pure or clean, and it revived the older Naga faith.

 

• Gaidinliu was honoured with a Padma Bhushan in 1982.

 

• Jadonang was her cousin and the first leader of the movement.

 

• The Naga Hills district of Assam was under the British, and Gaidinliu's movement spread among the Zeliangrong clans of Manipur, Nagaland and North Cachar Hills.

 

NOTE

 

• Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A (Option 2): This option treats the literacy claim as true and explaining the assertion, but the Heraka movement sought religious revival and political resistance, so R is false and cannot explain A.

 

• Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A (Option 3): This option agrees that both statements are true; the continuation of Heraka after Jadonang is true, but the literacy objective in R is incorrect, so the pair cannot both be true.

 

• A is false but R is true (Option 4): This option declares A false, but Rani Gaidinliu did continue the Heraka movement after Jadonang's execution, so A is a correct statement and the problem lies only in R.

question:
Assertion (A): The Indigo Revolt of 1859-60 took place in Bengal.

Reason (R): After the revolt, European planters shifted their operations to Bihar.

Choose the correct option.
option_1: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
option_2: A is true but R is false
option_3: A is false but R is true
option_4: Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
solution_text:
The correct answer is Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Assertion A is true: the Indigo Revolt (1859-60) broke out among cultivators in Bengal, especially in Nadia (नील विद्रोह — बंगाल)

 

• Reason R is also true: many planters moved their indigo business to Bihar after the Bengal troubles, and the tinkathia system there led to the Champaran Satyagraha in 1917.

 

• R is a consequence of the revolt and not an explanation of why it took place in Bengal, so it does not explain A.

 

• Therefore both are true but R is not the correct explanation.

 

• The cause of the revolt in Bengal was the planters' coercive contracts, whereas the planters' relocation to Bihar was a later consequence.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• The Indigo Commission of 1860 criticised the planters' coercive practices.

 

• Dinabandhu Mitra's Nil Darpan was the literary voice of the revolt.

 

• Champaran lies in north Bihar.

 

• Bihar's later indigo problem in Champaran was described by Gandhi's colleague Rajkumar Shukla, who invited him to the district in 1917.

 

NOTE

 

• Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A (Option 1): This option links R as the cause of A, but the shift of planters to Bihar happened after the Bengal revolt, so it cannot explain why the revolt occurred in Bengal.

 

• A is true but R is false (Option 2): This option calls R false, but historical accounts confirm that planters relocated to Bihar after the Bengal agitation, a shift that later produced the tinkathia grievances in Champaran.

 

• A is false but R is true (Option 3): This option calls A false, but the 1859-60 indigo agitation was centred in Bengal districts such as Nadia and Jessore, so the assertion is an accurate statement.

question:
Assertion (A): The Sanyasi Revolt (1763-1800) was one of the earliest major uprisings against British rule in eastern India.

Reason (R): It was caused by the introduction of the Permanent Settlement of 1793.

Choose the correct option.
option_1: A is true but R is false
option_2: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
option_3: Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
option_4: A is false but R is true
solution_text:
The correct answer is A is true but R is false.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Assertion A is true: the Sanyasi Revolt in Bengal and Bihar began in 1763 and is counted among the first major rebellions against Company rule (सन्यासी विद्रोह — 1763-1800)

 

• Reason R is false: the revolt began in 1763, thirty years before the Permanent Settlement (1793), and its causes were harsh revenue policy after Buxar and the famine of 1770.

 

• Cornwallis introduced the Permanent Settlement in Bengal and Bihar in 1793, when the movement was already declining.

 

• So the assertion stands but the reason fails.

 

• The Permanent Settlement is thus a later development that cannot explain the earlier sanyasi unrest.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• Majnu Shah and Bhavani Pathak led the movement.

 

• The settlement fixed revenue permanently with the zamindars.

 

• Anandamath preserved the memory of the revolt in literature.

 

• The Permanent Settlement was introduced in 1793 under Governor-General Cornwallis and covered Bengal, Bihar and Orissa.

 

• Cornwallis's arrangement made zamindars permanent owners who paid fixed revenue, a system that did not apply uniformly to the whole of India.

 

NOTE

 

• Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A (Option 2): This option accepts the Permanent Settlement as the cause, but that arrangement was introduced three decades after the revolt began, so it could not have caused it.

 

• Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A (Option 3): This option accepts both statements and denies only the explanation, but R itself is factually wrong because the Permanent Settlement of 1793 was introduced long after the revolt began in 1763.

 

• A is false but R is true (Option 4): This option declares A false, although the Sanyasi Revolt of 1763-1800 is widely regarded as one of the earliest major uprisings against Company rule in eastern India.

question:
Assertion (A): Birsa Munda led the Santhal Rebellion of 1855-56.

Reason (R): The Santhals rose against zamindars, moneylenders and British rule.

Choose the correct option.
option_1: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
option_2: Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
option_3: A is false but R is true
option_4: A is true but R is false
solution_text:
The correct answer is A is false but R is true.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Assertion A is false: the Santhal Rebellion (1855-56) was led by Sidhu, Kanhu, Chand and Bhairav Murmu, while Birsa Munda led the Munda Ulgulan of 1899-1900 (संथाल विद्रोह — मुर्मू बंधु)

 

• Reason R is true: the Santhals of the Rajmahal hills rebelled against zamindars, moneylenders and the British authorities who supported them.

 

• Birsa was not yet born in 1855, since he was born around 1875 at Ulihatu.

 

• Hence only R holds.

 

• Birsa Munda belongs to the Munda people, while the Santhals are a separate tribe, so the assertion confuses two different revolts.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• The Santhal region was constituted into a separate district in 1855-56.

 

• Birsa Munda's followers called him Bhagwan.

 

• Hul means revolt in the Santhali language.

 

• The Murmu brothers are honoured in Jharkhand, and Sido-Kanho-Birsha University in Dumka is named after Sidhu and Kanhu together with Birsa Munda.

 

• Hul is the Santhali word for revolt, and the rising is therefore also known as the Santhal Hul.

 

NOTE

 

• Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A (Option 1): This option accepts that Birsa led the Santhal rising and that R explains it, but Birsa was born about two decades after 1855, so assertion A is plainly false.

 

• Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A (Option 2): This option treats A as a true statement, but the Santhal leaders were the Murmu brothers, so no pairing of A and R can both be true.

 

• A is true but R is false (Option 4): This option says A is true, but Birsa Munda belonged to the Munda tribe and led a separate rebellion in 1899-1900; only the reason about zamindars and moneylenders is correct.

question: Which of the following pairs of revolt and leader is NOT correctly matched?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Rampa Rebellion - Budhu Bhagat.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The Rampa Rebellion (1922-24) was led by Alluri Sitarama Raju, not Budhu Bhagat, who was a leader of the Kol Revolt of 1831-32 (गलत जोड़ी — रम्पा विद्रोह)

 

• The Bhil Revolt (1818-46) in western India had chiefs such as Seva Ram, so that pair is correct.

 

• Kanhu Murmu was one of the Santhal leaders of 1855-56, so that pair is correct.

 

• Birsa Munda led the Munda Rebellion (Ulgulan) of 1899-1900, so that pair is also correct.

 

• The question asks for the wrongly matched pair, so each of the other three pairs is a standard factual match of leader and rebellion.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• Budhu Bhagat's movement occurred about ninety years before Rampa.

 

• Rampa was in Andhra, while the Kol Revolt was in Chotanagpur.

 

• Alluri Sitarama Raju used guerrilla tactics against the police.

 

• Kol Revolt's leaders also included Singrai and Bindrai Manki of the Munda tribe, along with Budhu Bhagat of the Oraon region.

 

NOTE

 

• Bhil Revolt - Seva Ram (Option 1): Seva Ram is indeed named as a Bhil chief who led the tribal uprising of western India in 1818-46, so this pair is correct and therefore is not the wrongly matched one.

 

• Santhal Rebellion - Kanhu Murmu (Option 2): Kanhu Murmu, along with his brother Sidhu, led the Santhals of the Rajmahal hills in 1855-56, so this pairing is accurate and cannot be the answer to a question seeking the incorrect pair.

 

• Munda Rebellion - Birsa Munda (Option 3): Birsa Munda was the leader of the Ulgulan of 1899-1900, so this pairing is accurate and does not answer a question asking for the incorrect pair.

question: Which of the following is NOT associated with Birsa Munda's movement?
option_3: Rajmahal Hills as the centre of the rebellion
solution_text:
The correct answer is Rajmahal Hills as the centre of the rebellion.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The Rajmahal Hills were the centre of the Santhal Rebellion (1855-56), and not of Birsa Munda's movement, which was centred in the Ranchi region of Chotanagpur (बिरसा आंदोलन — राजमहल नहीं)

 

• The movement was called the Ulgulan, meaning Great Tumult.

 

• It was directed against the exploitative dikus (outsiders), who took tribal land.

 

• Birsa also called for the establishment of Munda Raj, an independent rule of the Mundas.

 

• The Rajmahal Hills, in contrast, are the Santhal heartland, and this mix-up is a common distractor in examinations.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• Birsa died in Ranchi jail in 1900.

 

• The Chotanagpur Tenancy Act of 1908 followed his movement.

 

• He is revered with the title Dharti Aba.

 

• Birsa Munda's birthplace Ulihatu and the town of Khunti are today associated with his memory in Jharkhand's Khunti district.

 

• Khuntkatti villages were those cleared by the original Munda clans, and their members held land in a way that outsiders were not permitted to claim.

 

NOTE

 

• Ulgulan (Option 1): Ulgulan is the very name of Birsa Munda's rebellion of 1899-1900, so it is firmly associated with him and is not the item that falls outside his movement.

 

• Opposition to dikus (Option 2): Hostility to the dikus, meaning outsiders who seized Munda land, was the core of Birsa's message, so it is associated with the movement and not the exception.

 

• Munda Raj (Option 4): Munda Raj, the vision of self-rule for the Mundas, was one of his central aims, so it is associated with his movement and does not answer a question asking for the exception.

question: All of the following were leaders of the Santhal Rebellion EXCEPT
solution_text:
The correct answer is Birsa Munda.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Birsa Munda led the Munda Ulgulan of 1899-1900 and had no role in the Santhal Rebellion of 1855-56 (संथाल नेता नहीं — बिरसा मुंडा)

 

• Sidhu Murmu was the foremost leader of the Santhal uprising along with his brother Kanhu.

 

• Kanhu Murmu was another principal leader, who also became the face of the movement.

 

• Chand Murmu and Bhairav Murmu, the younger brothers, were also leaders of the rebellion.

 

• The question asks for the person who was not a Santhal leader, and Birsa Munda is the leader of a different tribe's revolt.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• The four Murmu brothers are remembered as heroes in Jharkhand.

 

• Birsa Munda was born two decades after the Santhal rising.

 

• The Santhal revolt began in Bhognadih village, which is in the Sahibganj area.

 

• Sahibganj, Dumka and Godda districts are core areas in which Santhal memories of the rebellion still persist.

 

NOTE

 

• Sidhu Murmu (Option 1): Sidhu Murmu was the main leader of the Santhal Rebellion in the Rajmahal hills, so he is included in the list of its leaders and is not the exception asked for.

 

• Kanhu Murmu (Option 3): Kanhu Murmu, Sidhu's brother, shared command of the Santhal Rebellion, so he belongs among the leaders and cannot be the one who was not a Santhal leader.

 

• Chand Murmu (Option 4): Chand Murmu, the third brother, is named in the notes as one of the Santhal leaders, so he does belong to the group and is not the exception.
